issues.legal_issue: A landlord who makes a prima facie showing that a third party is in exclusive possession of the premises shifts the burden to the tenant to explain that possession.
material_facts: The landlord alleged that the tenant had sublet or parted with possession of the premises to a third party.
The tenant said the third party was an employee who attended to customers, but did not substantiate that claim with evidence of salary or commission.
The evidence showed that the third party was using the premises for a business of his own.
issues.conclusion: The landlord bears the initial burden of showing the third party’s exclusive possession; once that is shown prima facie, the burden shifts to the tenant to explain the possession, and a failure to do so permits an inference of subletting for consideration.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1)(b) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 permits eviction where a tenant, without the landlord’s written consent, sublets, assigns or otherwise parts with possession of the premises. Under Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. S.B. Sardar Ranjit Singh, Kala v. Madho Parshad Vaidya, and Vaishakhi Ram v. Sanjeev Kumar Bhatiani, the landlord must initially prove subletting; a prima facie showing of a third party’s exclusive possession shifts the onus to the tenant to explain it. Direct proof of a concealed agreement or payment is not required, and the court may infer consideration from the circumstances.

predicates.subletting_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks eviction on the ground that the tenant sublet or parted with possession of the premises.
predicates.landlord_prima_facie_proves_third_party_: The landlord makes a prima facie showing that a third party, rather than the tenant, has exclusive possession of the premises.

issues.definition: In a proceeding seeking eviction for subletting, a prima facie showing of a third party’s exclusive possession means the tenant must explain that possession.

issues.legal_issue: Independent business activity by a third party in exclusive possession, left unexplained by the tenant, establishes subletting and supports eviction.
material_facts: The third party’s visiting cards identified his own jewellery business and gave the premises as its address.
A subscriber list associated the same premises and telephone number with a business previously conducted there by the third party.
The tenant asserted that the third party was an employee paid by commission, but produced no evidence of salary or commission.
The third party was responsible for opening and closing the shop and had admitted conducting business there.
issues.conclusion: The evidence established that the third party was in exclusive possession and conducting an independent business, and the tenant failed to rebut the resulting inference of subletting; the eviction order was therefore upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1)(b) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, subletting or otherwise parting with possession without the landlord’s written consent is a ground for eviction. Applying the burden-shifting principles in Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. S.B. Sardar Ranjit Singh, Kala v. Madho Parshad Vaidya, and Vaishakhi Ram v. Sanjeev Kumar Bhatiani, proof of exclusive possession shifts the onus to the tenant; failure to explain it permits an inference of subletting, even without direct proof of payment.

predicates.subletting_eviction_appeal: The case is an appeal in an eviction proceeding based on alleged subletting or parting with possession.
predicates.third_party_independent_business_evidenc: Evidence shows that a third party used the premises for an independent business and identified the premises as the business address.
predicates.tenant_fails_to_explain_exclusive_posses: After the third party’s exclusive possession is shown, the tenant does not substantiate an explanation for that possession.

issues.definition: In an appeal from an eviction proceeding, evidence of a third party’s independent business at the premises, together with the tenant’s failure to explain that party’s exclusive possession, supports upholding eviction for subletting.
